text: Consolidated governments. - In the Interim Report we proposed special rules to determine the commercial zones of consolidated governments and the terminal areas of carriers serving such municipalities. A consolidated government arises when a municipality consolidates all or substantially all of its governmental or corporate functions with the governmental and corporate functions vested in the county in which such municipality is located, creating a new governmental entity combining these functions. See Interpretation of Operating Authorities, 112 M.C.C. 829, 831 (1971). We noted that a number of cities have unified with their county governments, including Baton Rouge, La., Miami and Jacksonville, Fla., Carson City, Nev., Indianapolis, Ind., Columbus, Ga., Lexington, Ky., and Nashville, Tenn., and that we have previously concluded that these consolidated governments constitute municipalities for the purposes of section 203(b) (8) of the Act. Interpretation of Operating Rights, supra, at p. 841. In those instances where we have been asked to define the zones of such municipalities, we have concluded that the commercial zone includes all points within the involved county and no points beyond. See Indianapolis, Ind., Commercial Zone, 115 M.C.C. 893 (1972). We stated our belief that this should be the general rule and requested comments from interested parties.
